proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 5(i), the comparison with the test function ψ₊ (1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ ψ₊ ≤ 1_{B̄_{1+ε''}(0)}) which gives the lower density bound; Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(3), and Ch. 4, 4.10(1).
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P; η_ρ(z) := ρ⁻¹(z − x) (Chapter03.blowUpMap x ρ); ω_n := unitBallVolume n = volume(B_1(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ), ℝⁿ = Euclid n.
1. (Reduction.) Since n ≥ 1, ω_n is the volume of a bounded set, so ω_n < ∞; hence c < ω_n forces c < ∞. If c = 0 the claim is trivial. Otherwise treat c as a positive real. Since (1 + ε)ⁿ → 1 as ε ↓ 0 and c < ω_n, choose ε > 0 with c·(1 + ε)ⁿ < ω_n.
2. (Test function.) Let ψ(z) := max{0, min{1, (1 + ε − |z|)/ε}}. ψ is continuous, 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1, ψ = 1 on B̄_1(0), and ψ = 0 outside B̄_{1+ε}(0); in particular ψ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).
3. (The limit integral is at least ω_n.) dim Q = n. Fix an orthonormal basis of Q; it yields a linear isometry j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with image Q (j = inclusion ∘ (basis representation)⁻¹). Hausdorff measure is invariant under isometries (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and on ℝⁿ, μHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Since j maps the open unit ball of ℝⁿ onto Q ∩ B_1(0), Hⁿ(Q ∩ B_1(0)) = volume(B_1(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ) = ω_n. Likewise Hⁿ⌞Q is finite on compact sets (pull back to ℝⁿ), so ψ is Hⁿ⌞Q-integrable. As ψ ≥ 0 and ψ = 1 on B_1(0): L := ∫_Q ψ dHⁿ ≥ ∫_{Q∩B_1(0)} ψ dHⁿ = Hⁿ(Q ∩ B_1(0)) = ω_n > c(1 + ε)ⁿ.
   By HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q applied to f = ψ, a(ρ) := ∫_{η_ρ(M)} ψ dHⁿ → L as ρ ↓ 0. Hence there is ρ₁ > 0 such that ofReal(a(ρ)) > c(1 + ε)ⁿ for all ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁).
4. (Upper bound for the blow-up integral.) Fix ρ > 0 and let λ := Hⁿ⌞η_ρ(M). Since ψ ≥ 0 is continuous, ∫ψ dλ = (∫⁻ofReal(ψ)dλ).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae; this holds whether or not ψ is λ-integrable), so ofReal(a(ρ)) ≤ ∫⁻ofReal(ψ)dλ (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal_le) ≤ λ(B̄_{1+ε}(0)) = Hⁿ(B̄_{1+ε}(0) ∩ η_ρ(M)), using ofReal(ψ) ≤ 1_{B̄_{1+ε}(0)}. Moreover B̄_{1+ε}(0) ∩ η_ρ(M) = η_ρ(B̄_{(1+ε)ρ}(x) ∩ M), and η_ρ is the translation z ↦ z − x (an isometry) followed by the homothety of ratio ρ⁻¹, so Hⁿ(η_ρ(S)) = ρ^{−n}Hⁿ(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^P (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image). Therefore ofReal(a(ρ)) ≤ ofReal(ρ⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{(1+ε)ρ}(x)).
5. (Conclusion.) For ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁), steps 3 and 4 give c(1 + ε)ⁿ ≤ ρ^{−n}Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{(1+ε)ρ}(x)), i.e. c·((1 + ε)ρ)ⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{(1+ε)ρ}(x)). Given ρ' ∈ (0, (1 + ε)ρ₁), apply this with ρ := ρ'/(1 + ε): c·ρ'ⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{ρ'}(x)). Thus the claim holds with ρ₀ := (1 + ε)ρ₁; in filter form, the map ρ' ↦ ρ'/(1 + ε) tends to 0⁺ along 𝓝[>] 0, so the eventual statement transfers. ∎
